title: Establish component organization and auto-layout standards for Figma library
creator: Maya Hernandez
description: Goal: Create a clear, enforceable set of organization and auto-layout standards for the Figma component library so designers and engineers can reliably consume components and token exports. This work is focused on: 1) consistent variant structure and naming (for programmatic mapping to the runtime), 2) canonical auto-layout rules for common primitives (buttons, rows, cards, tables, charts) to avoid fragile resizing, and 3) a lightweight publishing checklist that prevents regressions to token mapping and layer names used in downstream exports. Background: recent regressions in token exports and inconsistent layer ordering caused multiple front-end bugs and longer integration cycles. This ticket scopes the standards doc, fixes in the core button/table/chart components, and a publish checklist for releases.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Variant naming follows pattern <component>/<state>/<size> (examples included) for all primary primitives
A2: All buttons, table cells, and chart frames use defined auto-layout presets (axis, padding, spacing, alignment) documented in the standards doc
A3: Tokens referenced by components map 1:1 to tokens.json keys used by the platform build (no ambiguous layer names)
A4: Publish checklist is exercised by at least one release candidate without regressions (QA signoff recorded)
A5: Confluence standards doc and Figma library file are linked from this ticket and approved by Design Lead and a frontend engineer
tasks: T1: Draft standards doc with examples and anti-patterns
T2: Audit current library for components that violate auto-layout presets (generate list)
T3: Apply auto-layout fixes to button, table row, and basic chart container components
T4: Normalize variant names and flatten nested variants where possible
T5: Create publish checklist and automation note for token export
T6: Run release-candidate with QA and capture integration notes for engineering
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Hernandez: Created ticket after triage call. Noted repeated frontend bugs caused by changed layer names and inconsistent auto-layout frames. Punted deep token refactor to separate follow-up ticket.

2026-02-12 Arjun Patel: Preliminary audit completed — 42 components flagged. Major offenders: primary button variants with nested frames, table cell components with manual spacing inside auto-layout, and chart containers missing explicit min-width behavior. Uploaded CSV to drive.

2026-02-15 Ethan Cooper (FE eng): Reviewed proposed variant naming. Agreed on pattern component/state/size. Asked to avoid using spaces and to use kebab-case for programmatic parsing. Suggested adding a version token to component metadata (eg. v1.0) to help rollbacks.

2026-02-17 Maya Hernandez: Updated standards doc with kebab-case requirement and examples. Decided to keep disabled/hover/focus as top-level variant axes instead of nested groups for easier instance swapping. Added examples for chart container auto-layout behavior when axis labels overflow.

2026-02-19 Arjun Patel: Began applying fixes to primary button and table row components. Replaced several absolute-positioned icons with auto-layout-aligned icon slots. Left notes in Figma file for components that require engineering follow-up (token key changes).

2026-02-21 Naomi Blake (Design Lead): Reviewed and gave conditional approval. Requested that we include a short QA checklist for engineers verifying token-to-layer mappings and that the publish process requires a freeze of token key names for the release window.

2026-02-22 Arjun Patel: Ran a release-candidate locally using tokens exported from the modified library. Found two mismatches (layer name typos) — fixed and re-exported. QA checklist executed and attached below. Planning final publish on 2026-02-25 pending PM signoff.

2026-02-23 Maya Hernandez: Added retro notes: keep future work for 'token alias reconciliation' as separate ticket; log all breaking token changes in release changelog. Marking this ticket as In Progress while we complete the final publish steps.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Flattening variants increases the number of sibling variants but simplifies programmatic mapping — chosen in favor of runtime stability
Tradeoff: Enforcing strict kebab-case and token freezes reduces design agility during the release window but prevents costly frontend rollbacks
release_notes: Library 2026.03 will include standardized auto-layout presets for buttons, rows, and chart containers; variant naming normalization; and a publish checklist to lock token keynames during release
integration_followups: ENG-2813: Add parser support for kebab-case variant names in the UI runtime
ENG-2891: Improve token export validation in CI to detect layer name mismatches
